title: Generators (function*, yield)
description: A `function*` declaration returns a generator — a lazy iterator you advance with `.next()`, pausing at each `yield`.

notes: The asterisk attaches to the keyword: `function* name()`, not `function *name()` by convention.
Calling a generator function does NOT run its body — it returns a generator object. The body runs lazily on `.next()`.
Each `.next()` returns `{ value, done }`. After the final yield, the next call returns `{ value: undefined, done: true }`.

questions.q: What does calling a generator function (e.g. `counter()`) actually return?
options: A generator object (iterator) — the body has not run yet
An array of all yielded values
A Promise that resolves to the yields
questions.explain: Generator calls return an iterator immediately; the body runs lazily.

questions.q: What is the shape of the object returned by `.next()`?
options: { value, done, index } — index tracks how many yields have fired
Just the yielded value — `done` is signalled by throwing StopIteration
A Promise resolving to { value, done } — `.next()` is always async

questions.q: After the last `yield` runs, what does the next `.next()` call return?
questions.explain: Once the function completes without further yields, value is undefined and done flips to true.
